s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital and facial syndrome with multinodular proliferation and giant cells
key_facts: History of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
Treated with 4 cycles of ABVC and 3060 cGY radiation
Previous excisions of left upper eyelid mass
Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells
Increased mitotic activity
Positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme on immunohistochemistry
MRI shows lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the PALB2 gene

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme on immunohistochemistry

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multinodular proliferation and giant cells, with increased mitotic activity

shortlist.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, with increased mitotic activity

shortlist.label: Giant Cell Reparative Granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, with orbital involvement

raw.rationale: The histopathology showing a multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, along with positive CD68 and negative CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme on immunohistochemistry, is most consistent with a Giant Cell Tumor. The presence of increased mitotic activity and the specific genetic finding of a splicing variant in the PALB2 gene also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Erdheim-Chester Disease
rejected.why: Typically involves multiple systems and has a distinct histological pattern with foamy histiocytes and Touton giant cells, not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman Disease
rejected.why: Characterized by emperipolesis and positive S100 staining, which is not present in this case.

rejected.label: Langerhans Cell Histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically has positive CD1a and S100 staining, which is not seen in this case.

rejected.label: Giant Cell Reparative Granuloma
rejected.why: Usually occurs in the jaw bones and has a distinct radiological appearance, not consistent with the orbital and intracranial involvement in this case.
